chunks.title: SYLVA AG

Software architecture, code reviews, project planning, team leadership, and development. chunks.title: CARRE
chunks.text: CARRE. Research contribution. 2014-2016. Application and ontology development within research on patient empowerment and shared decision making for cardiorenal disease. At Democritus University of Thrace, I contributed to the Risk Data Entry System V2, Educational Resources Ontology, and Educational Data Aggregator, combining healthcare information modelling with practical software development. Risk data entry, Educational Resources Ontology, and Educational Data Aggregator. Technologies: HTML5, NodeJS, AngularJS, Docker, Dokku, GruntJS, Gulp, MongoDB, Virtuoso RDF server, SPARQL, OWL, Bioportal API, Jasmine.

chunks.title: CARRE
chunks.text: CARRE was a research project on personalized patient empowerment and shared decision making for cardiorenal disease and comorbidities. I contributed at Democritus University of Thrace from 2014 to 2016.

chunks.title: CARRE
chunks.text: My work covered the Risk Data Entry System V2, development of the Educational Resources Ontology, and the Educational Data Aggregator. These contributions combined application development with the representation and aggregation of healthcare educational information.

chunks.title: CARRE

chunks.title: CARRE

chunks.title: ThrombUS+
chunks.text: ThrombUS+. Research participation. Start: 2024. Research participation spanning wearable sensor networks, DVT risk-estimation tasks, and system integration. My recorded involvement includes lower-limb activity sensing, wearable integration and signal quality, as well as central intelligence software, communications, security, and privacy. These describe my participation in the research programme, without implying clinical validation. Participation in wearable-network, risk-estimation, signal-quality, and integration tasks. Technologies: .

chunks.title: ThrombUS+
chunks.text: ThrombUS+ is a research project investigating a wearable system for continuous monitoring, risk prediction, and immediate alerts for deep vein thrombosis at the point of care. This describes the project's research aim, not an established clinical result. My participation is recorded as beginning in 2024.

chunks.title: ThrombUS+
chunks.text: My recorded participation spans three work packages: the wearable sensor network, automated DVT risk estimation and detection and prevention, and integration and validation. The scope below identifies task involvement rather than claiming sole ownership or completion of every task.

chunks.title: ThrombUS+
chunks.text: Wearable-system tasks cover a lower-limb activity sensor network, wearable development and sensor integration, and testing with signal-quality and performance enhancements. These are tasks T4.3, T4.4, and T4.5.

chunks.title: ThrombUS+
chunks.text: Tasks T5.1 through T5.5 cover DVT detection using wearable ultrasound, impedance and light plethysmography, personalized risk estimation using patient profile and activity, a serious game for risk prevention, and extended-reality operator or user guidance.

chunks.title: ThrombUS+
chunks.text: My recorded involvement also includes T6.4, software integration and development of a central intelligence module and app, and T6.5, hardware and software integration, communications, security, and privacy.

chunks.title: ThrombUS+
chunks.text: The recorded contribution spans wearable systems, risk-estimation research, and software integration. The common thread is participation across the interfaces between sensing, application software, and the broader research system.

chunks.title: About Nikolaos Portokallidis
chunks.text: I work across software architecture and hands-on delivery, with depth in healthcare informatics and experience across education, SaaS, sustainability, workplace software, and media. My work has ranged from technical leadership for an educational platform to research contributions in healthcare knowledge representation, educational-data aggregation, clinical protocols, and wearable systems. I am interested in the point where a complex domain becomes software people can use. At SYLVA AG, I combined architecture and development with code reviews, planning, and technical guidance. Earlier work on CARRE and Electronic Clinical Protocols brought application development together with ontologies, linked data, and healthcare information. My background in mathematics and postgraduate study in informatics and the Internet of Things supports work across applications, information models, and connected systems. Earlier educational projects, Lexikratis and Arithmosthenis, involved software and voice-over infrastructure for children with dyslexia and mathematical learning difficulties.
